summary: Agents pass execute timeouts in milliseconds; the tool refuses them (63 wasted round-trips over 10 runs)
description:
[claude] Found in the 11-05 cross-run analysis (comment on ANVIL-62).

**Symptom:** the agent (mostly subagents) calls `execute` with `timeout=120000` or `360000`, meaning milliseconds. deepagents' FilesystemMiddleware reads the value as seconds and refuses it: `Error: timeout 120000s exceeds maximum allowed (3600s).` The agent then retries the same command without a timeout. Every configure and every build pays one extra model round-trip.

**Count** (`tool.result` events containing "exceeds maximum allowed"):

| Run | Count |
|---|---|
| 8e9cec14 | 20 |
| 750cffd7 | 8 |
| e115a19f (today's offline TC1) | 7 |
| 7772117c | 6 |
| 170c75eb, 6d9317d3, a62f1830 | 5 each |
| 825ae133 | 4 |
| 30467063 | 2 |
| ef37dd40 | 1 |

That's **63 in total**. Each one costs a full model call with the whole context (main averages 20-27K input tokens per call) plus a turn of latency.

**Fix** (host side, in our tool layer, not a prompt rule):

* Normalise before the middleware sees the value: if `timeout > max` and `timeout >= 1000`, treat it as milliseconds (`timeout // 1000`), clamped to the max. Note it in the tool result so the model learns the unit.
* State the unit in the `execute` tool description ("timeout: seconds, max 3600").
* Also record `duration_ms` on `sandbox.exec` events. Today only `tool.result` has it, so `anvil.analyze` still marks every command time `~` (estimated); this was a gap in ANVIL-83.

**Acceptance:**

* A unit test where `execute(timeout=120000)` runs with 120 s.
* The next real run shows 0 "exceeds maximum allowed" results.
* `anvil.analyze` shows exact command times (no `~`).
